meanings.note: Male sibling. Common masculine noun meaning 'brother, cousin' in everyday Russian.
in двоюродный/троюродный брат, often shortened to брат

examples.text: Мой старший брат живёт в Москве.
examples.trans: My older brother lives in Moscow.

examples.text: А это брат Всеволод. Мы очень переживаем.
examples.trans: And this is cousin Vsevolod. We're very worried.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

'взять на работу' = to give someone a job

examples.text: Вот и возьмите на работу Галилея.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'Voronezh', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Сказал, Москва деревня, а Воронеж город возможностей.
examples.trans: He said Moscow is a village and Voronezh is a city of opportunity.

examples.text: Да, в Воронеже все любят рыбу!
examples.trans: Yes, in Voronezh everyone loves fish!

examples.text: В Воронеже трюфели — это только конфеты!
examples.trans: In Voronezh, truffles are only candies!

meanings.note: Pointing at something. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.
Emphasis. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Я тебе говорю = I'm telling you. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.
usually the short form: я готов (m), я готова (f)
emphatic at the start of a sentence

meanings.note: давай + 1st person plural or infinitive
давай + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'готовка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'preparation' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Заготовка на завтра сама себя сделает?
Заготовка на завтра сама себя не сделает!
examples.trans: Tomorrow's prep will not do itself!

examples.text: Утром все повара начинают день с чистки и нарезки заготовок.
examples.trans: In the morning all the cooks start the day by cleaning and slicing prep ingredients.

meanings.note: A fact or a person. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Imperative: извини / извините. Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to excuse; (imperative) sorry, excuse me', paired with 'извинять'.

Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to excuse; (imperative) sorry, excuse me', paired with 'извинять'.

examples.trans: Thank you, Marina. Sorry, I'm in a hurry.

meanings.en: to fix, to correct, to put right
meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'править'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to fix, to correct', paired with 'исправлять'.

examples.trans: Excuse us, we will fix everything.

examples.text: Ученик быстро исправил ошибку в тетради.
examples.trans: The pupil quickly corrected the mistake in his notebook.

examples.text: Да, вы знаете, это очень серьёзная операция. Мы всё исправим. До свидания!
examples.trans: Yes, you know, it is a very serious operation. We'll fix everything. Goodbye!

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'period', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Ладно, пусть завтра приходит на испытательный срок.
examples.trans: Alright, let him come tomorrow for a trial period.

examples.text: Денис, уже полчаса, как идёт испытательный срок.
examples.trans: Denis, your trial period started half an hour ago.

meanings.note: in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Agreeing, often reluctantly. Core Russian part meaning 'all right, OK' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: лучший в мире = the best in the world
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('best; better').

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'lyova', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Лёв, ты же сам говорил, что рук не хватает.
examples.trans: Lyova, you said yourself that we are short-handed.

meanings.note: Agrees with the thing owned. Core Russian det meaning 'my, mine' in everyday speech.
+ prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: + dative of the person + infinitive: мне нужно позвонить

examples.trans: I need to make a call.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
For masculine and neuter things. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.
Inanimate masculine noun. Common masculine noun meaning 'experience, experiment' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You will need my rich experience.
This life experience is very valuable.

examples.text: А вот тут вам понадобится мой опыт.
examples.trans: And right here you will need my experience.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'ветственный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('responsible, crucial').

examples.trans: This is a very responsible assignment.

examples.text: Хорошо, давайте три. Под мою личную ответственность.
examples.trans: All right, let's say three. On my personal responsibility.

meanings.note: Irregular plural повара. Common masculine noun meaning 'cook, chef' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

meanings.note: Disappoint expectations. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'вести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to let down, fail', paired with 'подводить'.

examples.trans: I will never let you down.

examples.text: Надёжный друг никогда не подведёт в беде.
examples.trans: A reliable friend will never let you down in trouble.

examples.text: Подведём итоги твоей первой рабочей недели.
examples.trans: Let us sum up your first work week.

meanings.note: + с + instrumental. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'знакомиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to meet, to get acquainted', paired with 'знакомиться'.

examples.text: А как вы с ней познакомились?
examples.trans: And how did you meet her?
She was the one who met me!

examples.text: Это она со мной познакомилась! Ходила вокруг меня, как акула.
examples.trans: She was the one who met me! She circled around me like a shark.

meanings.note: regularly, or as a general invitation: приходи!

examples.trans: If you change your mind, come back. The job is waiting.

meanings.note: + 3rd person verb: 'пусть строят' = let them build

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: 'на работе' = at work. Common feminine noun meaning 'work, job' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'work, job' in everyday Russian.
работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Dining establishment. Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: They called from the Italian restaurant.
In the evening they went to a restaurant.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.en: to decide, to make up one's mind
meanings.note: Решать, что делать. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to decide, to solve', paired with 'решить'.

examples.trans: Decide for yourselves what to do.

examples.text: Вот он, телефон! Сами решайте, что делать. Без меня!
examples.trans: Here it is, the phone! Decide for yourselves what to do. Without me!

meanings.note: Жать руку = to shake hands. Common feminine noun meaning 'hand; arm' in everyday Russian.
Сам, сама, само, сами. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself (myself, yourself...)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

справиться.gloss: to manage, to cope, to handle

meanings.note: often + с + instrumental, or used absolutely

examples.text: Мы за два года тут не справимся.
examples.trans: We won't manage here in two years.

examples.text: Конечно, не справитесь. Вы же не я.
examples.trans: Of course you won't manage. You're not me, after all.

examples.text: Мы обязательно справимся и с этим.
examples.trans: We will definitely cope with this too.

meanings.en: to ask (a question, or someone: спросить у кого-то)
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'просить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to ask', paired with 'спрашивать'.

examples.text: А спросите у него, куда он дел компьютерный класс.
examples.trans: Ask him where he put the computer lab.

examples.text: Да? А спросите у него, куда он дел компьютерный класс.
examples.trans: Really? Then ask him where he put the computer lab.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'whom'.

examples.text: Кого спросить-то? Теперь ты всё решаешь.
examples.trans: Ask whom? Now you decide everything here.
Sorry that I left. I let everyone down.

meanings.note: Второй срок = a second term. Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'term, period' in everyday Russian.
Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'term, period' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: At the start of a question. Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.
Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: As opposed to before. Core Russian adv meaning 'now (from now on)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Я точно не помню его адрес.
examples.trans: I don't remember his exact address.

examples.text: Точно, полиция была! А что с машиной?
examples.trans: That's right, the police were there! And what about the car?

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

уехать.gloss: to leave, to go away (by vehicle)

meanings.note: By car, train etc. Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to leave, to go away (by vehicle)', paired with 'уезжать'.

examples.trans: I'll be gone for an hour.

examples.text: Слушай, я уеду на полтора часа. Ты с Викой посиди, понял?
examples.trans: Listen, I'm going out for an hour and a half. You stay with Vika, got it?

meanings.note: 'хватать за горло' = grab by the throat
Impersonal, with the genitive. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to grab, to seize', paired with 'схватить'.

examples.text: Почему он меня всё время за горло хватает?
examples.trans: Why does he keep grabbing me by the throat?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях
Plural люди, a different word. Common masculine noun meaning 'person; (pl) people' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
